web_evidence.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets: Chapter One excerpt
web_evidence.note: Scholastic's authorized excerpt opens with sustained narration about the Dursleys and Harry from an external third-person position.

web_evidence.title: Word Magic: Defining Harry Potter's World in New Terms
web_evidence.note: This East Carolina University master's thesis analyzes an interior Chamber of Secrets passage and explicitly identifies Rowling's technique as third-person limited through Harry.

web_evidence.title: Discovering by Analysis: Harry Potter and Youth Fantasy
web_evidence.note: This Kent State University master's research paper states that the Harry Potter series employs third-person point of view; its study includes the first four novels, including Chamber of Secrets.

web_evidence.title: First, Second and Third Person Explained
web_evidence.note: Merriam-Webster explicitly describes Rowling's Harry Potter narration as third-person limited and demonstrates it with an interior passage from Chamber of Secrets that refers to Harry as he while revealing his thoughts.

web_evidence.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets: Key Facts
web_evidence.note: The book-level guide identifies the narrator as third person following Harry and explains that the narrative reveals Harry's private thoughts.

search_log: Searched for authorized excerpts using queries including "Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets J.K. Rowling official excerpt" and exact opening language; found and inspected Scholastic's Chapter One excerpt.

Searched for explicit narrator and point-of-view analysis using "Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets third person point of view scholarly" and related queries; opened the East Carolina University and ERIC theses, Merriam-Webster, SparkNotes, and LitCharts results.
Checked Google Books for a preview; the opened edition reported that no preview was available, so its catalog description was not used as person evidence.

Ran targeted searches for epistolary form, diary/frame narrative, multiple narrators, alternating point of view, and first-person narration; results consistently described third-person narration, while the diary was discussed as an embedded magical object rather than the novel's constitutive form.

Searched exact clipped quotations to resolve local structure: q00616 was identified as Ron's joke, q00620 as text inside a Daily Prophet clipping, and q00621 as the writing on the wall; none is base narration.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating, close third person centered on Harry. Multiple sampled interior passages externally name Harry while reporting his thoughts, feelings, and perceptions, and these agree with an authorized Scholastic opening, two scholarly sources, and explicit whole-book reference descriptions. First- and second-person forms in the sample occur in dialogue, verse, warnings, or embedded documents; Tom Riddle's diary and the Daily Prophet clipping are local diegetic material rather than sustained alternative narration. No credible evidence of first-person, second-person, or alternating base sections was found. The authorized excerpt covers only the opening, but the interior quotes and scholarly analyses remove that scope limitation.
